clue.text: I'd return runaway criminal

indicators.note: something runaway is out of control, so the letters before it scatter into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to come back to recapture an escaped convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' and 'runaway' both suggest an escape and its sequel, but INTRUDER is simply the letters of I'D RETURN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder breaks into a property unlawfully, so is a kind of criminal such as a burglar or trespasser.

clue.text: Vice overcoming naughty literary sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing overcoming another sits on top of it, so the first piece is written above the second

blocks.note: a vice is a sin
naughty means bad

explanation.surface: Wickedness gets the better of mischief, as a moral tale might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the seafaring hero of tales in the Arabian Nights, so a sailor from literature.

clue.text: Woman keeping in time with instrument  …

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the woman's name holds the next word

blocks.note: a woman's name
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A musician keeps in time with the rest of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping in time' reads as one musical phrase, but 'in' is the letters held inside CLARE. The ellipsis links this clue to the next, which also ends with an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument played with a single reed.

clue.text: …  instrument revealed by party swapping Liberal for Tory leader

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another exchanges them, so one letter of the party is replaced by another
a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the UK Labour Party
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political party trades a Liberal for the Conservative leader, as in a coalition reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour, Liberal and Tory are three British political parties; the L of LABOUR is replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabour is a small drum played with one hand, often alongside a pipe, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Gang encountering Italian outlaw

blocks.note: a band is a group or gang
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A criminal gang runs into an Italian outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, so an outlaw is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Remove a vital part of Shed's insides during ball

indicators.note: the insides of a word are its interior letters, dropping the first and last
something happening during another event falls inside it, so these letters go into the next word

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the four-letter word
a bead is a small ball

explanation.surface: Something essential is taken from inside a shed while a dance is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance but is a small round bead. 'Remove a vital part of' sounds vague, yet the head is the most vital part.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead is to cut off the head, removing an organ no one can survive without.

clue.text: Setter employed in factory is easy to persuade

indicators.note: someone employed in a workplace is inside it, so this letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: A factory worker is a pushover when asked to do things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword compiler, who is I in the clue's own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant literally means bendable, and figuratively describes a compliant person readily influenced.

clue.text: Permanent reminder of soldiers' nocturnal entertainment?

blocks.note: first meaning: an inked design on the skin that never fades
second meaning: a military display, originally an evening drum signal calling troops back to quarters

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a soldier's night out leaving a lasting mark; the military sense is a show of marching bands such as the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Body ink lasts for life, and the military display grew out of an evening drum call, hence its link with night.

clue.text: Eve and Cain all upset about gossip primarily based on the gospels

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the names and word before it are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Eve and her son Cain are distressed by rumours, a Bible story with a soap-opera twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joining Eve and Cain is only a link; its letters are not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical comes from the Greek for good news, the gospel, and describes teaching grounded in those books.

clue.text: Angelfish swallowing monarch

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so the fish holds the monarch

blocks.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: An angelfish gulps down a monarch butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angelfish' looks like one word, but the definition is 'Angel' and the wordplay starts with 'fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is one of the orders of angels, often pictured as a winged child.

clue.text: Clergyman turning to speaker for drink

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the other way, so the title is read backwards

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
the mouth is what speaks

explanation.surface: A vicar turns to the person at the lectern to ask for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning to speaker' sounds like the clergyman facing someone; 'turning' acts on REV alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif or in cocktails.

clue.text: Home help is very cross about source of ironing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anger word goes round the letter
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: mad means very angry
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The cleaner is furious about the pile of ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic servant, someone employed to help with housework.

clue.text: Loud noise welcoming popular bloke getting married in restaurant

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the noise holds the next word

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise
in means fashionable or popular
the man at a wedding

explanation.surface: A rowdy restaurant greets a well-liked bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining room, as in a hotel, is a room where meals are served, much like a restaurant.

clue.text: Throat surgery transformed chatty Romeo

indicators.note: something transformed is changed in form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A talkative lover is silenced by an operation on his throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is a word in the fodder here, not the NATO alphabet letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracheotomy is an incision into the windpipe, an operation on the throat to help breathing.

clue.text: Shoemakers with balls

blocks.note: first meaning: people who mend shoes
second meaning: British slang for nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' and the second meaning are both British slang for rubbish talk, from rhyming slang on 'cobblers' awls'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers are shoe repairers, and in British slang the same word is an exclamation for nonsense.

clue.text: Chap goes to small wood to get tree

blocks.note: a chap is a man
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: A man heads into a copse to fetch a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical tree growing in coastal swamps on stilt-like roots.

clue.text: Animal taking trouble to attack

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A beast goes out of its way to charge at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, a formal verb for attacking.

clue.text: Talk of food crop in The Archers?

indicators.note: talk of means as spoken, so the word wanted is one heard rather than seen

blocks.note: cereal is a grain crop grown for food

explanation.surface: Farmers in a radio soap discuss their wheat harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming village, so food crops really are its talk. The question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story told in instalments, and this radio programme is the longest-running drama of that kind.

clue.text: Gathering sees Wally and bride finally married with ostentatious display

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: a wally is British slang for a fool
the last letter of the word
M is the abbreviation for married
bling is showy jewellery or flashy display

explanation.surface: At a flashy wedding, guests watch an idiot and the bride tie the knot amid much glitz.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering and assembling both describe bringing people or things together in one place.

clue.text: Joshua finally leaving Frank for another man

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the name is kept
something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out of the next word

blocks.note: the last letter of the name
frank and earnest both mean sincere

explanation.surface: Joshua finally walks out on Frank and takes up with another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning sincere, which neatly sets up a pun on Ernest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a male first name, and the clue's 'another' contrasts him with the apparent Frank and Joshua.

clue.text: Lass with raw material aplenty

blocks.note: a gal is a girl or lass
ore is the raw material mined for metal

explanation.surface: A girl comes with an abundance of raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore follows a noun to mean in abundance, the same job aplenty does.

clue.text: Those voting against speaker's good judgement?

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard rather than read, so the word wanted only sounds right

blocks.note: a nose for something is a knack for judging it well

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House wonders whether the votes against are sound sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the parliamentary chair who calls the ayes and the noes, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary votes the noes are the members voting against a motion, opposed to the ayes.

clue.text: Animal with go ruined plant

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature on the move tramples a garden shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering shrub or tree, prized for its large showy blooms.

clue.text: Bird accepted by poet

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
in can mean accepted, as in being in with a crowd

explanation.surface: A poet takes in a songbird, as poets so often do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepted by' reads as one piece of wordplay; here 'by' only joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was an English poet, author of The Whitsun Weddings and This Be The Verse.

clue.text: Sin about to produce a healthy glow?

blocks.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Wickedness, it is suggested, puts colour in your cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: lustre is shine, which suits glowing good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft gleam or sheen, like the shine of glossy hair or bright eyes.

clue.text: It makes no sense to push learner

blocks.note: to drive is to push forward
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone protests that shoving a learner around is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push learner' sounds like a driving instructor's task, which is the joke behind the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is foolish, meaningless talk, the stuff that makes no sense at all.
